claim: Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,\|\cdot\|_{3,3/2})\) be the real Day--James plane with \[\|(x,y)\|_{3,3/2}=\begin{cases}(|x|^3+|y|^3)^{1/3},&xy\ge0,\\(|x|^{3/2}+|y|^{3/2})^{2/3},&xy\le0.\end{cases}\] Then the exact Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance is \[d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X,\ell_2^2)=\frac{2^{5/6}}{\sqrt3},\qquad d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X,\ell_2^2)^2=\frac{2^{5/3}}{3}.\] An optimal Euclidean pullback norm, up to positive scaling, is \[|(x,y)|_*^2=\frac{5x^2-2xy+5y^2}{4}.\]
integrity: The proof is analytic and global. The bundled numerical replay only checks arithmetic and sampled values; it is not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is only for the real two-dimensional Day--James plane \(\ell_3-\ell_{3/2}\). It does not determine all conjugate exponents or classify every optimal map. The 2018 primary von Neumann--Jordan paper was not directly available in the bounded full-text check; its theorem and hypotheses were checked through the later authors' full-text survey.
title: Exact Hilbert distance of the cubic conjugate Day--James plane
